question: In triangle ABC, angle A = 35°, angle C = 88°, and side AB = 31 cm. Explain how to find the length of side AC using the sine formula, and calculate it correct to 3 significant figures.
referenceAnswer: First, find angle B using the angle sum of a triangle: $B = 180^\circ - 35^\circ - 88^\circ = 57^\circ$. Then apply the sine formula: $\frac{AC}{\sin B} = \frac{AB}{\sin C}$, so $AC = \frac{31 \sin 57^\circ}{\sin 88^\circ} \approx 26.0$ cm.
evidence: A + B + C = 180° → 35° + B + 88° = 180° → B = 57°. By the sine formula, $\frac{AC}{\sin 57^\circ} = \frac{31 \text{ cm}}{\sin 88^\circ}$ → $AC = \frac{31 \sin 57^\circ}{\sin 88^\circ} = 26.0 \text{ cm, cor. to 3 sig. fig.}$

question: Triangle ABC has angles A = 123°, B = 22°, and side AB = 19 cm (opposite angle C). Find angle C and explain why BC is longer than AC using the sine formula and angle sizes.
referenceAnswer: Angle C = 180° − 123° − 22° = 35°. Since BC is opposite angle A (123°) and AC is opposite angle B (22°), and larger angles face longer sides, BC > AC. This is confirmed by the sine formula: $BC = \frac{19 \sin 123^\circ}{\sin 35^\circ} \approx 27.8$ cm, while $AC = \frac{19 \sin 22^\circ}{\sin 35^\circ} \approx 12.4$ cm.
evidence: C = 35°. $\frac{AC}{\sin 22^\circ} = \frac{19 \text{ cm}}{\sin 35^\circ}$ → AC ≈ 12.4 cm. $\frac{BC}{\sin 123^\circ} = \frac{19 \text{ cm}}{\sin 35^\circ}$ → BC ≈ 27.8 cm.

question: In triangle ABC, angle A = 41°, angle C = 87°, and side AC = 22 cm (opposite angle B). Calculate the length of side BC, showing your steps using the sine formula.
referenceAnswer: First, find angle B = 180° − 41° − 87° = 52°. Since BC is opposite angle A, use $\frac{BC}{\sin 41^\circ} = \frac{22}{\sin 52^\circ}$. So $BC = \frac{22 \sin 41^\circ}{\sin 52^\circ} \approx 18.3$ cm.
evidence: B = 52°. $\frac{BC}{\sin 41^\circ} = \frac{22 \text{ cm}}{\sin 52^\circ}$ → $BC = \frac{22 \sin 41^\circ}{\sin 52^\circ} = 18.3 \text{ cm, cor. to 3 sig. fig.}$

question: Given $\frac{7 \text{ cm}}{\sin \theta} = \frac{9.5 \text{ cm}}{\sin 61^\circ}$, solve for $\theta$ and explain why only one acute solution is valid in this context.
referenceAnswer: Rearrange to get $\sin \theta = \frac{7 \sin 61^\circ}{9.5} \approx 0.644$, so $\theta \approx \sin^{-1}(0.644) \approx 40.1^\circ$. Since the diagram (No. 10) shows an acute angle and no indication of ambiguity (e.g., no second possible obtuse angle given side–angle–side configuration), only the acute solution is accepted.

question: In a triangle, side lengths 11 cm and 7 cm are opposite angles $\theta$ and $37^\circ$ respectively. Given that $\theta$ is acute, find $\theta$ using the sine formula and verify that the calculated value satisfies the acute condition.
referenceAnswer: Apply the sine formula: $\frac{11}{\sin \theta} = \frac{7}{\sin 37^\circ}$, so $\sin \theta = \frac{11 \sin 37^\circ}{7} \approx 0.946$. Then $\theta = \sin^{-1}(0.946) \approx 71.0^\circ$, which is acute — satisfying the given condition.
evidence: $\frac{11 \text{ cm}}{\sin \theta} = \frac{7 \text{ cm}}{\sin 37^\circ}$ → $\sin \theta = \frac{11 \sin 37^\circ}{7}$ → $\theta = 71.0^\circ$, cor. to 3 sig. fig. $\theta$ is acute.
